If your COVID-19 test result is positive:  
- Contact your VA health care team right away (or your provider).  
- If you need treatment, start it early—some treatments must start within 5 days of your first symptoms.  
- Isolate for at least 5 days from when your symptoms started or from when you tested positive; if you can’t fully isolate, wear a well-fitting mask around others for at least 5 days.  
- Tell anyone you had close contact with in the past few days.  
- Monitor symptoms; if you have emergency signs (e.g., trouble breathing or chest pain/pressure), call 911 or get help immediately.

For a solar eclipse, you need proper eye protection: eclipse glasses (safe solar viewing glasses) or a solar filter. Keep the glasses/filters on during the partial eclipse, and only remove them briefly during totality when the Moon completely blocks the Sun. If you don’t have eclipse glasses, use an indirect viewing method like a pinhole projector. For photography, a camera is optional (even a phone works); a tripod can help stabilize shots in low light, and a delayed shutter release timer can reduce camera shake.

MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment) is a tech demo on the Mars 2020 Perseverance rover that tests producing oxygen from the Martian atmosphere. Its main job is to produce oxygen from the Martian carbon-dioxide atmosphere, using an electrolyzer (like a fuel cell running in reverse). Primary attributes: located inside the rover (front, right side), mass about 37.7 lb (17.1 kg) on Earth, power 300 watts, and oxygen production up to 0.022 lb/hour (up to 10 g/hour). Functionality: runs intermittently for about one hour of oxygen production per experiment over the mission duration.
